reasons.reason: When two circles touch from the outside, the segment joining their centers runs straight through the point of contact, so its length is one radius plus the other, three and five together.
Tangent circles meet at a single point, and the gap between their centers is set by how far the larger radius reaches past the smaller one, so taking three from five gives the distance.

The circle's area is pi times the radius squared, and with the radius equal to half the side, the circle takes up pi over two of the square, so the region between them is one minus that.
The square has area four and the inscribed circle has radius one, so its area is pi; the circle fills pi over four of the square, and the corners outside it make up the rest.
Completing the square on the y terms turns plus eight y into y plus four squared, and because the circle passes through the origin, the radius matches that four-unit shift along the vertical axis.
